To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

i) linear state-feedback controllers can be designed that are able to control the transient energy growth of subcritical Poiseuille channel flow, ii) the transient growth of subcritical flow cannot be eliminated completely by means of linear state-feedback controllers, iii) the performance of such controllers can be improved by employing different velocity components at the channel walls as actuators and sensors, and iv) the transient growth can be suppressed more efficiently by employing a nonlinear state-feedback controller.

transient growth in plane Poiseuill flow cannot be suppressed via linear state-feedback control and that the use of a linear state-feedback control law that directly targets the dominant transient energy growth mechanism is more effective in terms of control performance than the use of a standard linear-quadratic optimal controller.

transient energy growth in plane Poiseuill flow cannot be completely suppressed by means of linear state-feedback control and that the performance of linear state-feedback controllers is highly dependent on the choice of velocity component as wall actuation, with the streamwise velocity component being most effective.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a control strategy to suppress the transient energy growth of the flow.
the development of control techniques for turbulent flows.
the development and analysis of control techniques for the stabilization of the laminar flow in a plane channel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the case at hand, linear state-feedback controllers are able to suppress transient growth and, thus, to delay the onset of transition.

linear state feedback control is not capable to suppress transient growth in subcritical Poiseuille flows, but it can be used to delay its onset and to reduce its magnitude, provided that a proper choice of control velocity component is made.

linear control of the transient growth mechanism in subcritical plane channel flow can be effective, but only in the linearized setting, where the control input can be directly targeted to the transient growth mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we show that it is possible to design linear state-feedback controllers that suppress the transient growth in subcritical Poiseuille flows and that such controllers can be designed for a large number of velocity components.

the transient growth mechanism can be effectively suppressed by means of state-feedback control, but that the control performance is limited by the fact that the control input is restricted to the velocity components at the walls.
the transient energy growth is a very sensitive mechanism to control.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given initial condition, the transient energy growth is not completely suppressed by linear state-feedback control.
the transient growth of subcritical plane Poisueuille flow can be suppressed via linear feedback control.

the linear state-feedback controller is able to significantly suppress the transient growth of the flow, and that it is possible to design a state-feedback controller that targets a specific transient growth mechanism.
